Question kind: invariant_properties

Question:
Use the full test suite in `tests/qa/testcase.py`, class `TestFilterSchemasDualDictGrowthLoopInvariantSuiteQA` (22 tests). Each test invokes `cfnlint.jsonschema._filter.FunctionFilter.filter` (which delegates to the private `_filter_schemas` method) on JSON schemas of varying composition -- standard-only, group-only, and mixed (with the group key first, last, and alternating); schemas with ``$ref`` (cfnLint short-circuit), schemas that exercise the post-loop ``object``/``patternProperties`` and ``array``/``items`` arms, and one empty schema. Inside `_filter_schemas` (file `src/cfnlint/jsonschema/_filter.py`), two locally-declared dicts ``standard_schema`` and ``group_schema`` are populated by the loop `for key, value in schema.items():` (line 80): each iteration appends to exactly one of the two dicts, depending on whether `key in self.group_functions`. Across the entire test-suite execution, consider every Python `line` event of `_filter_schemas` whose `lineno == 80` (the for-loop header, fired once per iteration immediately BEFORE the body runs). At every such event, is the candidate loop invariant `len(standard_schema) >= len(group_schema)` always held? Return JSON as `{\"invariant_exists\": <bool>}` where `true` means the invariant holds at every observed event and `false` means it does not.

{"invariant_exists":"bool"}

- files/tests/qa/testcase.py

From `_filter_schemas`:

- `standard_schema = {}` and `group_schema = {}` are initialized before the loop.
- At line 80, `for key, value in schema.items():` iterates in insertion order.
- Each iteration body adds the current key to exactly one dict:
  - group key → `group_schema[key] = value`
  - otherwise → `standard_schema[key] = value`
- No other mutations to either dict occur until after the loop ends at line 85.

So at each visit to line 80 after the first, the lengths reflect exactly the counts of previously processed standard vs group keys from the schema prefix already traversed.

That means the candidate invariant `len(standard_schema) >= len(group_schema)` would fail whenever some already-processed prefix contains more group keys than standard keys. I can already see that from the tests:
- `{"required": ["x"]}`: on the second loop-header visit (before processing any hypothetical next item, or more precisely the next header after first body when there is another item) there isn’t one because only one key exists, so this test alone doesn’t disprove it.
- But `{"required": ["x"], "minItems": 1}` does: after processing the first key `required`, the next time line 80 is reached, lengths are `0` and `1`, so `0 >= 1` is false.
- Likewise many other tests start with one or more group keys.

To be thorough, I’ll also read the parser helper only if needed, but the decisive logic is already in the test inputs and `_filter_schemas`. Since the question is specifically about the full suite and line-80 events, the existence of even one such test with a second iteration after a leading group key is enough to make the invariant false. I’ll quickly inspect `parser.py` only to confirm there isn’t any alternate test discovery or transformation of inputs, then I’ll stop.
